The long blade rends the darkness.

Assassin handles the weapon, nearly two meters in length, with perfect freedom. Saber has yet to take a single step within his reach.

Saber has yet to be able to close in on her enemy that freely swings his longsword.

セイバーとアサシンの間合いの差は一メートル。
その、たった数歩分の石段を駆け上がる事さえ、セイバーには出来なかった。

“Kh…!”

Unable to evade completely, she is driven backward.

The distance between them refuses to close.

One meter separates Saber’s reach from Assassin’s.

Only a few steps of stone lie between them, yet Saber cannot advance even that far.

“Kuh……!”

The distance between the two does not shrink.
There is one meter between Saber and Assassin.
But Saber is unable to climb the few steps.

She bites her lip.

There is no time to continue this skirmish.

She surpasses him in raw strength. If she uses her magical energy and the force of her sword as a shield, he is not an opponent she cannot overwhelm.

One blow.

If she resolves herself to suffer a single blow, she can subdue him with ease.

She surpasses him in power.
She can overpower him if she uses her magical energy and her sword as a shield.
Just one blow.

甘んじて一撃を受けた瞬間、彼女はアサシンに踏み込み、敵を両断する自信がある。

If she refuses to flinch from a lesser wound, he will never have the opportunity to strike twice.

The instant she accepts the blow, she is confident she can enter Assassin’s guard and cleave him in two.

If she does not allow the wound to slow her, there will be no second attack.
She can surely slash Assassin after she receives his blow.

If that single blow is certain to take her head, she cannot force her way through.

Every stroke of the Servant before her is such a blow.

He never feints. Every attack seeks her life.

Retreat is the only means of defending against it.

The narrow terrain prevents her from circling him, and his consummate skill will not allow her to advance.

But…
If the attack is to come for her neck, she cannot overpower him.
All of this Servant’s attacks are of that kind.
All are meant to take her life.
Retreat is the only defense against them.
She cannot move forward because of the enemy’s technique, and the geographical disadvantage does not allow her to move to either side.

She charges.

She runs.

“…Impressive. As expected from Saber’s sword. I thought it would be able to take a few blows, but it was bent after just one…!”
Sparks fly off.
The swords try to push each other away.

“He blocked it…? Assassin blocked my sword…?”

Assassin’s blade is fragile.

It may be a masterpiece said to cut even iron, but it remains a weapon forged by human hands. It cannot compare with her sword, wrought through an art beyond mankind.

If the two weapons met head-on in a contest of strength, the long blade would unquestionably shatter.

Assassin knew this. That was why he had always turned her sword aside and forced her back by striking at her body rather than her weapon.

“Assassin blocked my sword…?”
Assassin’s sword is fragile.
It is a good sword that can even cut steel, but it is made by a human. It cannot even be compared to her sword that is not made by men.
His longsword would be pulverized if he used his power to strike back at the oncoming attack.
That is why Assassin has parried the attacks and pushed back Saber by attacking her body instead of her sword until now.

However thoroughly the blade has been tempered, whatever resilience Assassin’s own skill may lend it, no mere sword can withstand Saber’s blow.

The long blade that caught her strike is bent at its core.

It can no longer retain the deadly edge it possessed until now.

But Assassin blocked this attack.
Assassin’s sword cannot block Saber’s attack no matter how strong he is.
The longsword that blocked Saber’s attack is bent.
There’s no way it’s as sharp as it was before.

*…Can I win? Can I defeat this man without injury…?*

She asks herself as she bears down upon Assassin’s long sword.

That hesitation becomes carelessness.

There was a purpose in Assassin’s decision to receive her blade.

Before she understands what it was, he has maneuvered her into position.
pages.mirrorMoon:
‘I can beat him? Can I beat him without a scratch…?’
Saber asks herself while she pushes back Assassin’s longsword.
That question becomes an opening.
There is a reason why Assassin blocked her sword.
She is standing in that position before she realizes it.

They had been separated by the upper and lower steps. Now they stand level with one another.

Without even realizing it, Saber has been drawn sideways onto perfectly flat ground.

“……!”
Their positions are different.
They are now standing on the same level.
Before she realizes it, Saber has been forced to fight sideways.

She cannot press forward.

The swordsman is simply captivated by the eyes of an opponent driven to the brink, still searching for one stroke that will overturn her fate.

pages.en:
—She advances through a sea of rotting flesh.

The pond is less than a meter deep.

Its floor is thickly carpeted with the mass, so in truth she sinks only to her knees.

“This—this is beyond disgusting! God…!”

She curses between ragged breaths.

Each step brings the sickening sensation of crushing a swarm of insects beneath her feet.

The carrion clinging to her skin is exactly what it appears to be. If she stops moving, it begins to harden around her, trying to draw her inside.

“Kh…! Oh, damn it all…!”

She tears it away by force and presses onward.

Slosh. Slosh. Squelch.

No sane person could endure wading through its contents.

*After this, butchering a whole cow would be nothing,* Rin Tohsaka decides with grim resignation.

And so she grows accustomed even to this labor.

The situation is so desperate that she would be unable to move if she did not regard it as mere work, but at least the sight no longer wounds her spirit.

“Kh… ah, hah, ah—”

This, however, is not something she can endure by changing her state of mind.

Her body grows hotter with every step.

The carrion that wraps around her legs invades her nerves the instant it touches her. By the time she tears it off, the poison has already entered her system.

A curse.

This tangible embodiment of malice toward others is like a violent ague.

Touching it brings immediate illness.

It invades the nerves, steals strength, and boils the brain. By the first step, its effects are lethal.

An ordinary person would stop moving after the second and collapse into the rotting flesh.

What happened after that, she does not know.

She has no desire to imagine whether they would suffocate or become another part of the carrion.

Her head, already burning above forty degrees, is hardly capable of imagining anything at all.

“Ghh—damn… you—”

She fights desperately to steady her faltering feet and swaying body, forcing herself onward.

…Rin did not leap into the carrion entirely without a plan.

She swallowed two of her remaining treasured jewels and committed all the magical energy stored within them to a defensive membrane.

If this curse is crystallized magical energy, then surrounding herself with sufficiently powerful energy should repel it—

“Kh—this is… bad—”

…Her vision warps.

Her prediction was correct, but she misjudged the scale.

The jewels she swallowed might as well have been paper.

This is not something a human being can resist.

No person could pass through it without having something taken from them.

…Here, only one thing keeps her alive:

the strength she can muster against her own failing self.

“It’s—hot—God… At this rate, jumping into a sea of fire would be cooler.”

In fact, protected by her jewels, she could leap into a sea of fire without harm.

The instant the meaningless complaint leaves her mouth—

“——”

her own flippancy infuriates her, and her resolve returns.

No. That is not true at all.

This suffering cannot begin to compare, and she has no right to make so light of it.

Through her fevered haze, she listens to the clash of swords behind her.

…She can no longer see either combatant.

Perhaps Shirou Emiya drew him away. Perhaps he was simply driven back with no means of resisting.

Whichever it was, their battle seems to have moved into the temple grounds.

“—Just a little farther. I’ll make it in one rush, so until then…”

She runs.

Even so, she can manage little more than walking speed, but she keeps her legs moving.

She forces her way through the rotting flesh.

Breathing raggedly and without dignity, she reaches toward the mound.

“There—!”

She climbs almost on all fours.

The mountain of flesh is solid beneath her hands.
